title: The Deep End
subtitle: A Pool in Laurel Canyon, a Report Written Too Early, Can Fourteen

setting.name: Los Angeles, Wednesday 24 to Friday 26 September 1947
setting.description: Three days after a death the city has already decided was an accident. The party works from wherever they have hidden Vivian (Mags Fennimore's apartment, Dr. Roland Pryor's clinic on Central Avenue, a motor court in Glendale) and moves between Abel Kurland's house in Laurel Canyon, the coroner's basement in the Hall of Justice downtown, the switchboard room of a Hollywood answering service, the LAPD's Hollywood Division station on Wilcox Avenue, a bank on Hollywood Boulevard, a committee investigator's hotel suite, and the Castellane lot, where Kurland hid the negatives in the one building on the lot built to survive a fire. Lt. Frank Dolan has closed the case by Wednesday noon, the newspapers print 'SUBPOENAED WRITER DROWNS' on Thursday, and the studio sends flowers. Everyone the party talks to has a reason to want this to be an accident, and one of them is the man paying the party's expenses.
setting.atmosphere: Chlorine and eucalyptus. The coroner's basement, cold as a meat locker, with a radio playing somewhere down the corridor. A switchboard room full of women in headsets plugging and unplugging cords and saying 'Mr. Kurland's residence' fifty times an hour. A police station with a ceiling fan that doesn't work. Newspaper headlines that turn a man into a cautionary tale overnight. Grief: Vivian's, Roz's if she is in the party, and the players' own if they liked Kurland. Then fear, as the clues begin to point at the kindest man they have met in the case. Keep the tone procedural and tight. This is the scenario where the players get to be detectives.

keyLocations.name: Kurland's House and Pool, Lookout Mountain
keyLocations.description: The shingled house, the study, the wet bar, and the kidney-shaped pool with its flagstone deck, concrete coping, underwater light and a skimmer basket at the shallow end that the pool man empties on Mondays. On Wednesday morning, the police come and go by ten; after that the house is sealed with a strip of paper across the door that a penknife can lift.
features: The study: the Royal typewriter with a page still in the roller, the stack of Dry Wells, the unopened subpoena, the corkboard
The wet bar and the kitchen: two clean martini glasses in the cupboard over the stove, where the coffee cups go
The pool deck: a dark stain on the coping at the deep end, a scuff on the flagstones, the diving board
The skimmer basket, full of leaves and something paper
encounters: Lt. Frank Dolan and two Crooked Cops on Wednesday morning, who want the party gone and the scene 'tidied'
Lupe Ortega, the maid, who arrives at nine for her Wednesday shift and finds the police in the kitchen
Lyle Preston of the committee, Thursday, who comes with a federal marshal to look for Kurland's papers and finds the party already there
secrets: CLUE K1b (core, anyone who looks at the deck): the stain on the coping is blood and hair at the deep end, two feet from the diving board; the board itself is clean and dry. A man who dives drunk off a board hits the bottom or the board, not the coping beside it; a man who hits the coping going backwards was standing on the deck facing someone. His reading glasses are on the bottom eight feet from the body, lens cracked: they came off at the edge, not in a dive.

CLUE K1b, continued (core, Lupe Ortega): 'Mr. Abel never put the glasses over the stove. Never. He was very particular, the glasses go in the bar. Somebody washed these and didn't know.' Two glasses: he had a guest.

CLUE K1d and K3a (core, read the typewriter): the page in the roller is a scene from Dry Wells, typed that night, the last lines: 'FADE IN. INT. THE VAULT - NIGHT. The cans stacked to the ceiling. ELLEN takes down can fourteen, the rushes nobody will ever print, and holds it like a baby. ELLEN: It's all in here. Every one of them. Now we bargain.' A man planning to bargain is not a man planning to drown himself.

CLUE K2c (core, anyone who checks the skimmer basket or asks the pool man, who empties it on Mondays and has not been back): a paper currency band, wet, printed 'PACIFIC UNION TRUST & SAVINGS, HOLLYWOOD OFFICE, $5,000', with a teller's initials and Tuesday's date stamped on it.
The gin bottle on the deck is empty and wiped clean of prints (Forensics DC 12 with a fingerprint kit, or Eddie Navarro asking the police lab): a drunk does not wipe his own bottle.
The subpoena is still sealed. If anyone opens it: Kurland, Abel J., to appear before the committee in Washington on 21 October.

keyLocations.name: The Coroner's Basement, Hall of Justice
keyLocations.description: The county coroner's rooms below the Hall of Justice downtown: a corridor of green tile, a cold room with steel drawers, an autopsy room with a drain in the floor, and the deputy coroners' office with its typewriters and a pot of terrible coffee. Deputy Coroner Walter Ness, forty, wire glasses, a wife and three children in Inglewood and a dentist's bill he could not pay until Wednesday morning.
features: The body in drawer 31, released to the family on Friday
Ness's typed report and the autopsy log book on the clerk's desk, with its time column
The back corridor and loading dock where the undertakers' wagons come in
encounters: Walter Ness, who is frightened, ashamed and bad at lying
A morgue attendant who will let a doctor or a reporter see a body for $20
Dr. Roland Pryor (companion), whom the party can bring in as 'the family's physician' with a letter from Vivian or Kurland's ex-wife
secrets: CLUE K1a (core, any look at the body by Dr. Pryor or anyone proficient in Forensics or Medicine): a depressed fracture at the back of the skull with grit from concrete in it, and bruising on the left jaw from a fist; fresh skinned knuckles on Kurland's own right hand. He was hit, fell backwards, and hit his head, and the water in his lungs says he was alive when he went in. With Forensics DC 14: the stomach contents smell of coffee, not gin; he had perhaps one drink.

CLUE K1c (core, reading the log book or Ness's report): Ness's report, 'accidental drowning, acute alcoholic intoxication', is typed and signed with the time 8:40 a.m. Wednesday. The autopsy log shows the post-mortem began at 10:15 a.m. The verdict was written before anyone looked inside him.

Leaning on Ness (Intimidation DC 13, or Persuasion DC 12 if the party promises to keep him out of it): 'Lieutenant Dolan brought me the report already typed and an envelope. Two hundred dollars. He said it was a kindness to the family. My Annie needed her teeth.' He does not know who paid Dolan. He will repeat it to a grand jury only if the party protects him (+1 Heat if they push him in public).

keyLocations.name: Hollywood Personal Answering Service
keyLocations.description: Two floors up over a florist on Cahuenga Boulevard: a room of sixteen women at a long switchboard, each with forty clients' lines, taking messages for writers, actors, doctors and bookmakers on pink slips in pigeonholes. The chief operator, Pearl Duchesne, sixty, has had Kurland's line since 1941 and liked him.
features: The message pigeonholes and the operators' call sheets, kept for thirty days
Pearl's desk, a candy dish, a photograph of a son in Navy whites
A back stair to the alley
encounters: Pearl Duchesne, who will help anyone who loved Mr. Kurland and nobody who calls him 'the deceased'
If Shay has been told where the party is going: a studio lawyer, Mr. Cobb, already in Pearl's office asking for the call sheets 'for the estate'
secrets: CLUE K2b (core, Pearl's call sheet for Tuesday): '10:40 p.m. Call from Mr. Shay's office, Castellane. Message: Mr. S. coming up tonight with what was discussed.' And in Pearl's handwriting below: 'Mr. K. said hold all calls after eleven, he had the devil coming for a drink.'

CLUE K3b (core): a message Kurland left on Monday afternoon for 'Miss Pell, when she calls': 'Tell Dot the rushes are safe where they keep the fire.' Vivian, Agnes or anyone who knows a studio knows: the nitrate vault is the fireproof building.

Red herring: Monday 22 September, 4:15 p.m., Pearl connected 'Miss Pell' to Kurland and heard, before she closed the key, Miss Pell say: 'Then I'll do it without you, Abel.' Pearl will say this unhappily.
Red herring: Tuesday 6:20 p.m. Pearl's note: 'Mr. K. called to say if a Mr. Preston calls again tell him to go to hell. Exact words.'

keyLocations.name: LAPD Hollywood Division, Wilcox Avenue
keyLocations.description: A brick station house with a front desk, a squad room upstairs, a ceiling fan that does not work and a coffee urn that does nothing else. Lt. Frank Dolan, fifty-five, runs the detectives. He has a lake cabin at Arrowhead on a lieutenant's pay.
features: The front desk and its log book: every call, every radio dispatch, every officer's phone-in, with the time
Dolan's glass-walled office and its filing cabinet
The squad room, where Det. Eddie Navarro (if a player character) has a desk by the window
encounters: Lt. Frank Dolan (Bent Detective), who calls the party in for a friendly chat once Heat reaches 3, and tells them, kindly, that the case is closed and so are they
Sgt. Mike Ferraro, the desk sergeant, who likes Eddie Navarro and dislikes Dolan, and who will show a page of the log book for $10 or a favour
secrets: CLUE K2e (core, the front-desk log for Wednesday 24 September): '6:50 a.m. Lt. Dolan phoned in from home: any Lookout Mountain business this a.m. to come to him personally.' Then: '7:04 a.m. Report of a drowning, 8290 Lookout Mtn. Ave., by pool service man.' Dolan knew there would be a body before there was one.

Eddie Navarro (player knowledge, or Insight DC 15 on Dolan): Dolan got a telephone call at home late on Tuesday night; his wife told the desk sergeant's wife at church that it woke the baby at ten past twelve.

Dolan will not crack. He is on Shay's payroll and has been for six years, and he would rather be killed by the studio than charged by the DA. What breaks him is proof he was paid, which belongs to kl-scenario-004.

keyLocations.name: Pacific Union Trust & Savings, Hollywood Office
keyLocations.description: A marble banking hall on Hollywood Boulevard with brass teller cages, a manager behind a rail, and the studio's accounts on the second floor. The teller whose initials are on the currency band is Miss Frances Kim, twenty-six, careful, who remembers every large cash withdrawal because the manager makes her count it twice.
features: The teller cages and the cash cage
The manager's desk and the studio accounts ledger
A side door onto Ivar Street
encounters: Mr. Lowell Brace, the manager, who does not discuss clients' business, and Miss Kim, who does not like being told what she saw
secrets: CLUE K2c, confirmed (Research DC 13 through the bank's records, a Persuasion DC 14 with Miss Kim, or Roz Keane's friend on the financial desk): on Tuesday 23 September at 2:30 p.m., Harlan Shay cashed a Castellane Pictures special-services cheque for $5,000 in fifties and hundreds. Miss Kim banded it herself with her initials. Shay was 'very calm and very polite and his hands were shaking'.
Shay redeposited $5,000 in cash on Wednesday morning at 9:05, in different bands. A man who carried $5,000 up a hill and brought it all back down did not buy what he went to buy.

keyLocations.name: The Castellane Lot: the Parking Office, Shay's Bungalow, the Nitrate Vault and the Back Lot
keyLocations.description: The studio, again, after hours. The parking office by the Gower gate assigns numbered windshield stickers by seniority. Shay's bungalow behind the commissary. Behind the film laboratory, sunk half underground in reinforced concrete with iron doors and a sprinkler system, the nitrate vault: forty small fireproof rooms holding every negative and print the studio owns, on a film stock that burns hot enough to melt steel and keeps burning underwater. Beyond it the back lot: the Western street, the New York street with its brownstones and elevated railway, the European village square, the lake three feet deep.
features: The parking office's register of numbered stickers
The vault keeper's key log, in a hut by the vault door; the vault's ventilation shafts and its single steel door
Room 14 in the vault, with can 14 on its third shelf, marked 'DRY WELLS / TESTS / DO NOT PRINT'
The back lot's sets, which are fronts with nothing behind them but scaffolding, ladders and catwalks; the studio police patrol on bicycles, and a guard dog is loosed after midnight
encounters: Harlan Shay in his bungalow, with a bandage on his right hand
Agnes Whitlow (companion), who can get the party into the vault keeper's hut

On Friday night at the vault: two studio police (Night Watchmen) and a Guard Dog, and either Shay's own men (two Crooked Cops on loan from Dolan, in plain clothes) or Tiny Bascombe and two Street Toughs from the Sirocco, or both, depending on what Shay and Ambler know
secrets: CLUE K2a, confirmed (core, the parking register): sticker No. 7, 'H. Shay, 1941 Packard 180 sedan, dark green'. Mrs. Ruiz saw No. 7 in Kurland's drive.

CLUE K2d (core, any meeting with Shay on Wednesday or Thursday): his right hand is bandaged across the knuckles; he says he caught it in a car door. And when the party first tells him 'Abel Kurland is dead', before anyone has said how, he says 'Drowned? Poor Abel. He never could swim when he'd been drinking.' Insight DC 12 catches the slip at once; otherwise the GM should remind the party of it later. Nobody had told him.
CLUE K3c (core, the vault keeper's key log, or Agnes): 'Mon 22 Sept, 3:10 p.m., A. Kurland, Rm 14, in 3:25.' Writers have no business in the vault; Kurland has no picture in production.

Can 14 holds a reel of genuine screen tests for Dry Wells, and wound inside the reel's core, in a glassine envelope, thirty-one 35mm negatives and a contact sheet: Councilmen Dwight Hollister and Ray Fenwick at the Sirocco card table, taking envelopes; Wendell Haig shaking hands with Hollister; and one frame of Harlan Shay handing Fenwick an envelope while Vivian Lark laughs at something off-camera. (These are clue M1a for kl-scenario-003.)

Nitrate: a dropped cigarette, a muzzle flash in the vault, or a thrown Molotov sets the room alight. Nitrate fire spreads to the next room in 1 round, deals 2d6 fire damage per round to anyone inside, and its fumes require a DC 12 Constitution save each round or be poisoned. The sprinklers come on in round 2 and do not put it out. Anyone who does not want to burn leaves by the steel door or the ventilation shaft (Athletics DC 12).

keyLocations.name: Lookout Mountain Avenue: the Neighbours
keyLocations.description: The hillside houses either side of Kurland's: a set designer's place with a Japanese garden, an old cowboy actor's ranch-style house, and the big Spanish house above, where a radio producer lives and his housekeeper, Mrs. Esperanza Ruiz, sits on the back steps at night with a cigarette because her employer does not allow smoking in the house.
features: Mrs. Ruiz's back steps, with a clear view down into Kurland's drive and pool
The narrow road with one place to turn a big car
encounters: Mrs. Esperanza Ruiz, who has already been asked nothing by the police and is offended by it
The set designer, Mr. Corliss, who heard shouting at six
secrets: CLUE K2a (core, anyone who asks Mrs. Ruiz): 'At eleven, a big car, dark green, a Packard, I know cars, my husband drove for the Pacific Electric, parked in the drive with no lights. A studio sticker in the window, the castle, number seven. A man in a light suit. I heard nothing; the radio was on. At half past eleven it went away without its lights until the turn.'

Red herring (core): Mr. Corliss heard a man shouting at Kurland's front door at six, 'You'll be sorry you didn't take this chance, Mr. Kurland', and saw a thin man in a dark suit with a briefcase. That is Lyle Preston of the committee, and he was at a dinner at the Sirocco with Harlan Shay from eight until half past ten.

synopsis: Abel Kurland is at the bottom of his pool, a committee subpoena unopened on his desk and an empty gin bottle on the deck, and by noon Lt. Frank Dolan and the coroner's office have ruled it an accident: a frightened man drank and fell in. The party, and Vivian, know better, and this is the scenario in which they prove it. The body shows a fist on the jaw and a fracture from the pool's coping, not the diving board; the glasses were washed and put in the wrong cupboard; the coroner's report was signed before the autopsy began; and the last page in Kurland's typewriter, written at a quarter past eleven, is a man planning to bargain. Then the clues start pointing somewhere nobody wants them to: a dark green Packard with studio sticker No. 7 in the drive at eleven, a call from 'Mr. Shay's office' logged by the answering service, a $5,000 currency band in the skimmer basket from the bank where Harlan Shay cashed a studio cheque that afternoon, a bandaged hand, a slip of the tongue, and a police lieutenant who called in about a body before anyone had found one. The client is the killer. Meanwhile Lyle Preston of the committee wants Kurland's papers, Royce Ambler wants the negatives, and Kurland's typewriter and his last message to Vivian point to the studio's nitrate vault. The scenario ends on Friday night on the Castellane back lot, with the party getting can 14 out of a building full of film that burns underwater, and holding photographs of two councilmen taking envelopes, and of Harlan Shay handing one over.
hook: By ten in the morning the house on Lookout Mountain is full of men in hats. The pool has been drained six inches so they could get him out, and Abel Kurland is under a grey blanket on the flagstones with his bare feet showing, and one of the men in hats is eating a doughnut. Lieutenant Frank Dolan of Hollywood Division, a big, slow, tidy man with a grey moustache, looks at the party for a long time before he speaks. 'Sad business,' he says. 'Man gets a subpoena, man has a drink, man has another, man goes for a swim. Happens every summer up here.' He brushes sugar off his tie. 'You folks were friends of his? Then you'll want to go home and be sad somewhere else. Coroner's already got it.' And as the party goes, they hear him say to his sergeant, not quite quietly enough: 'Call the studio. Tell them it's tidy.'

conclusions.conclusion: Abel Kurland was killed: struck, fallen and left to drown. It was not a drunken accident and not suicide.
clues: K1a: The body: a fist bruise on the jaw, a fracture from the concrete coping, coffee not gin (coroner's basement, Dr. Pryor)
K1b: The pool deck: blood on the coping beside the board, glasses off at the edge, two washed glasses in the wrong cupboard (Kurland's house, Lupe Ortega)
K1c: The coroner's report signed at 8:40, the autopsy begun at 10:15, and Ness's $200 (coroner's basement)
K1d: The page in the typewriter, written that night by a man planning to bargain (Kurland's study)

conclusions.conclusion: Harlan Shay, the party's client, was at the pool at eleven and is the man responsible for Kurland's death. (Proved beyond doubt only when he confesses or the negatives show him, but the party should have it by the end of this scenario.)
clues: K2a: Mrs. Ruiz saw a dark green Packard with studio sticker No. 7; the parking register gives No. 7 to Shay (neighbours, Castellane lot)
K2b: The answering service's 10:40 p.m. call from 'Mr. Shay's office' and 'the devil coming for a drink' (Hollywood Personal Answering Service)
K2c: The $5,000 currency band in the skimmer, and Shay's cash withdrawal and redeposit (Kurland's pool, the bank)
K2d: Shay's bandaged right hand and his slip, 'Drowned?' (Castellane lot)
K2e: Dolan's 6:50 a.m. phone-in before the body was reported, and his 12:10 a.m. call (Hollywood Division)

conclusions.conclusion: Kurland hid the Sirocco negatives in the Castellane nitrate vault, room 14, can 14.
clues: K3a: The typewriter page: 'can fourteen, the rushes nobody will ever print' (Kurland's study)
K3b: His message for Dot: 'the rushes are safe where they keep the fire' (answering service)
K3c: The vault key log: Kurland in room 14 on Monday afternoon (Castellane lot, Agnes Whitlow)

acts.title: Act 1: Tidy
acts.description: Wednesday 24 September. The pool, the police, the coroner and the studio's reaction. Let the party look at the scene before Dolan's men arrive if they came at dawn; afterwards they must talk their way in or come back when the house is sealed. Plant K1b, K1d and K2c at the house, then move the party to the coroner and to Shay.
objectives: Examine the pool and the house before the police tidy it
Get Vivian somewhere safe (she wants to see Abel; let her, and let it hurt)
Get a look at the body and the coroner's report

scenes.name: Before the Men in Hats
scenes.description: If the party arrived at dawn (kl-scenario-001, Act 3), they have about forty minutes alone with the scene before the pool man arrives at seven and the police at seven-thirty. Let them choose: call the police themselves, search, or both.
scenes.readAloud: The water is so still you can see the grain of the concrete on the bottom. A leaf turns slowly on the surface by the shallow end and goes into the skimmer's mouth. The deck is dry except for one dark place on the lip of the pool at the deep end, two feet from the board, where something has dried brown on the white coping, and a few short grey hairs are stuck in it. The house behind you is quiet. A typewriter in the study has a page in it, and the lamp is still on.

skillChecks.success: Bonus detail on K1b: the stain is blood from a scalp wound; the angle says he went over backwards from standing on the deck. The diving board's sandpaper is dry and clean. Whoever was here stood between him and the house.
skillChecks.failure: There is blood on the coping (core) and you are not sure what it means beyond that he hit his head.

skillChecks.success: The skimmer basket (K2c, core if checked): the wet paper band from Pacific Union Trust, $5,000, Tuesday's date. And the gin bottle is wiped: no prints, not even his.
skillChecks.failure: You find the band only if someone says they are checking the skimmer; otherwise Lupe Ortega finds it on Friday and keeps it for Vivian.

scenes.name: Lieutenant Dolan
scenes.description: Dolan arrives at seven-thirty with two detectives, takes charge, and tidies. He wants the party gone. If Eddie Navarro is a player character, Dolan is his boss and puts him on 'something else' at once. Dolan's kindness is the threat.
scenes.readAloud: Lieutenant Dolan walks round the pool once, slowly, with his hands in his pockets, the way a man walks round a used car he has already bought. He looks at the stain on the coping and then he looks at one of his detectives, who takes out a handkerchief and squats down by it. 'Man slipped,' Dolan says, to nobody. 'Wet deck.' The deck is bone dry.

skillChecks.success: Dolan is not curious. He has not asked a single question. He knew what this was before he got out of his car.
skillChecks.failure: Dolan is a lazy cop who wants an easy case closed before lunch.

skillChecks.success: You stay on the scene as 'the studio's people', and Dolan lets you, because the studio is a friend of the department. You see the detective wipe the coping with his handkerchief.
skillChecks.failure: You are escorted to your car. +1 Heat. Dolan takes your names.

scenes.name: Telling Harlan
scenes.description: The party tells Shay, in person or by telephone. The slip, the bandage, the grief: Shay is genuinely upset, and that makes it worse. He offers a bonus of $200 each to 'keep finding Vivian, and let the police handle Abel'.
scenes.readAloud: Shay listens with his eyes closed. When you say Abel Kurland is dead he opens them, and for a moment his face is completely empty, like a set when the lights go off. 'Drowned?' he says. 'Poor Abel. He never could swim when he'd been drinking.' He reaches for the coffee pot with his right hand, and there is a fresh white bandage across the knuckles. 'Car door,' he says, when he sees you see it. 'I'm getting old.'

skillChecks.success: K2d: nobody told him Kurland drowned. He said it before you did. And his grief is real, which is the worst thing about it.
skillChecks.failure: He is shaken and sad, an old friend of the dead man. Note what he said anyway; the GM will remind you.

encounters: Lt. Frank Dolan (Bent Detective) and two Crooked Cops at the scene; no fight unless the party is spectacularly foolish (+3 Heat and the city closes ranks)
Lupe Ortega, Kurland's maid, a witness and an ally

acts.title: Act 2: Accidental Drowning
acts.description: Wednesday afternoon to Friday afternoon. The legwork: the coroner's basement, the answering service, the neighbours, the desk log at Hollywood Division, the bank, and a committee investigator who wants the dead man's papers. The K2 clues accumulate. Run it as a sandbox; each location points to two others. Shay's offer of money, Preston's offer of a deal and Dolan's offer of a quiet life all arrive in this act.
objectives: Find out who was at the pool at eleven (K2)
Work out where Kurland hid the negatives (K3)
Deal with Lyle Preston and the federal marshal
Decide whether to keep reporting to Shay, and what to tell Vivian

scenes.name: Drawer Thirty-One
scenes.description: The coroner's basement and Walter Ness. Dr. Roland Pryor, if the party brings him, examines the body in ten minutes and says what he finds plainly.
scenes.readAloud: The cold room smells of formalin and floor cleaner. The attendant pulls drawer thirty-one out on its rollers with a long steel sigh and folds the sheet down to the chest without being asked, as if this is the part people usually want. Abel Kurland looks smaller dead, and older, and very surprised. There is a bruise along the left side of his jaw the colour of a plum.

skillChecks.success: With the core K1a findings: the stomach smells of coffee. He had one drink at most. The 'acute alcoholic intoxication' is a lie.
skillChecks.failure: The core findings stand: a fist, a fall, the coping. The gin question waits for Dr. Pryor.

skillChecks.success: Walter Ness breaks: Dolan brought the report pre-typed with an envelope, $200. He'll say it again if you protect him.
skillChecks.failure: Ness tells you to get out and calls Dolan. +1 Heat. (K1c, the times in the log book, is still core: the report was signed at 8:40 and the autopsy began at 10:15.)

scenes.name: Sixteen Women and a Switchboard
scenes.description: Pearl Duchesne at the answering service. She has everything: the 10:40 call, the devil coming for a drink, the message for Dot, and the two red herrings (Vivian's 'without you', Preston). Give them all.
scenes.readAloud: The switchboard is a long wall of little holes and brass-tipped cords, and in front of it sixteen women in headsets are talking at once in the same calm voice: 'Doctor Feld's office, he's with a patient', 'Mister Grant's residence, may I take a message', 'I'm sorry, he's on location'. At the end of the room a grey-haired woman with reading glasses on a chain looks at you over them and takes off her headset. 'You're about Mr. Kurland,' she says. 'I can always tell. People walk differently when it's about somebody dead.'

skillChecks.success: Pearl gives you the call sheets for Monday and Tuesday and tells you everything (K2b and K3b are core with any polite request; success adds that the 10:40 caller was a woman, Shay's secretary Miss Abernathy, whose voice Pearl knows from five years of calls).
skillChecks.failure: Pearl reads you the sheets but will not let you copy them. A studio lawyer is coming at four to take them 'for the estate'; get back before then.

scenes.name: The Desk Log
scenes.description: Hollywood Division, the front desk, Sgt. Mike Ferraro and the log book. If Eddie Navarro is in the party he can simply read it; others need $10 or a story.
scenes.readAloud: The desk log is a long canvas-bound book with a pencil on a string. Every line is a call, a time and a set of initials, in eight different handwritings, and the one at 6:50 on Wednesday morning is in the sergeant's own square capitals.

skillChecks.success: Ferraro, for $10 or for Eddie's sake, shows you K2e: Dolan phoned in at 6:50 a.m. to claim any Lookout Mountain business, fourteen minutes before the pool man reported the body. He adds, quietly, about the call that woke Dolan's baby at ten past twelve.
skillChecks.failure: Ferraro will not show the book to strangers. Eddie Navarro, Percy's favours or a $20 bill fix that. Nobody fixes it without Dolan hearing about it (+1 Heat).

scenes.name: Mr. Preston of the Committee
scenes.description: Lyle Preston, investigator for the House committee, comes to the party, or the party goes to his suite at the Hotel Cordova on Hollywood Boulevard. He wants Kurland's papers, especially anything with names from 1938. He is the obvious suspect and he did not do it; he has an alibi (dinner at the Sirocco with Shay until 10:30, which is itself a clue that Shay and Preston are close). He offers a deal: bring him the papers and nobody in the party will ever receive a subpoena.
scenes.readAloud: Preston is thin and pale and very well barbered, with a briefcase he never puts down and a Phi Beta Kappa key on his watch chain. He speaks softly, like a man in a library. 'I'm not interested in how Mr. Kurland died,' he says. 'I'm sorry he did. He might have been a very useful witness, if he had been sensible. What I'm interested in is who he knew. Lists. Letters. Names.' He smiles. 'I find that most people have a list of someone else's names somewhere in them. It's just a question of what they'd rather keep.'

skillChecks.success: Preston is telling the truth about not killing Kurland; he is genuinely annoyed that a witness has been wasted. He is also lying about one thing: he is not here only for names. He has heard the word Sirocco and he wants whatever Kurland had, to use on Bernard Castellane.
skillChecks.failure: Preston is exactly what he looks like, a frightening, polite man with a list.

skillChecks.success: You convince Preston that Kurland's papers were burned. He loses interest in the party for the rest of this scenario.
skillChecks.failure: Preston is now interested in the party. Each character who has a past (Roz's 1930s union card, Percy's clients, Ken's family's camp file) gets a polite telephone call. +1 Heat.

encounters: Lyle Preston and a Federal Agent (a deputy marshal) at Kurland's house on Thursday; they have a warrant for papers and will search the party's car if they can
Tiny Bascombe and two Street Toughs in a black '41 Buick, tailing the party from Thursday to see if they lead to the negatives (Stealth vs passive Perception; spotting them is Perception DC 14)
Dolan's friendly chat at Heat 3: two Crooked Cops in a radio car, a ride to Wilcox Avenue, a cup of coffee, and a warning

acts.title: Act 3: Can Fourteen
acts.description: Friday night 26 September. The party goes onto the Castellane lot after dark to get can 14 out of the nitrate vault. Who else is there depends on what the opposition knows: if the party has reported to Shay or been careless at the answering service, Shay's men (two plain-clothes Crooked Cops borrowed from Dolan) are waiting at the vault; if Tiny's Buick followed them, the Sirocco is coming over the back fence. Run it as a heist with a fire waiting to happen.
objectives: Get onto the lot after hours (Bunny's transport pass, Agnes's script-department key, Ken's security uniform, or the back fence on the Western street)
Get the vault key from the keeper's hut, or get through the ventilation shaft
Find room 14 and can 14 and get the negatives out
Get off the lot alive without setting the vault on fire, or survive it if someone does

scenes.name: The Back Lot at Night
scenes.description: Getting in. The back lot is a city of fronts: walk into a saloon on the Western street and you are standing in scaffolding. Studio police on bicycles every twenty minutes; a guard dog loosed at midnight.
scenes.readAloud: The New York street at night is the loneliest place in Los Angeles. Brownstones with nothing behind their doors, a newsstand with last year's papers, an elevated railway that stops in mid-air at the end of the block over a pile of lumber, and above it the real sky, with searchlights from a premiere somewhere on Wilshire wheeling slowly across it like the beams of a lighthouse that has lost the sea. A bicycle bell rings two streets away. Somewhere a dog barks once and is quiet.

skillChecks.success: Group check. The party crosses the back lot to the laboratory without the studio police seeing them.
skillChecks.failure: Group check. A Night Watchman on a bicycle sees a light and comes to look. Bluff (Deception DC 12; automatic success with Bunny, Ken or Agnes's studio pass), knock him out quietly (Blackjack from surprise: knockout blow), or run. +1 Heat if he raises the alarm.

skillChecks.success: The vault keeper's hut padlock opens. The key ring is on a nail and the key log is on the desk (K3c, if not already found).
skillChecks.failure: The padlock will not give. The ventilation shaft on the vault roof is the other way in (Athletics DC 12), and it is narrow and smells of vinegar.

scenes.name: Where They Keep the Fire
scenes.description: Inside the vault: a corridor of forty iron doors, each a small room of shelves and film cans. Room 14, third shelf, can 14. The negatives are in the reel's core. Then the opposition arrives.
scenes.readAloud: The vault is cold, colder than the night outside, and the air smells sharply of vinegar and old camphor. A corridor runs away under caged bulbs between iron doors stencilled with numbers. Every door has a sign: NO SMOKING. NO MATCHES. NO LIGHTS BUT THESE. NITRATE FILM CANNOT BE EXTINGUISHED. Room fourteen's door sticks, then gives. Inside, film cans are stacked to the ceiling like hatboxes, labelled in grease pencil, and on the third shelf one fresh label in typewriter capitals says DRY WELLS / TESTS / DO NOT PRINT.

skillChecks.success: The reel of screen tests, and inside its hollow core, the glassine envelope of negatives and a contact sheet. You can see faces on the contact sheet by the caged bulb: a card table, a man with an envelope, a man with a cigar, a woman laughing.
skillChecks.failure: Can 14 is a reel of film. You take the whole can, which is heavy and takes both hands; you find the envelope later.

skillChecks.success: You hear the steel door at the corridor's end open, and two men's voices, and a lighter click. Somebody has just lit a cigarette in a nitrate vault.
skillChecks.failure: The first you know is a voice at the door of room fourteen saying 'Mr. Shay would like that back, please', and a lighter's flame.

scenes.name: Burns Underwater
scenes.description: The confrontation in the vault and on the back lot. Shay's men want the can and no shooting; Tiny's men want the can and do not care. If anyone fires a gun in the vault, or the lighter goes into a room, the nitrate catches (see the nitrate rules in the vault's secrets). The escape runs out across the back lot: the Western street, the lake, the New York street's elevated railway. Studio police and then the Hollywood fire department converge.
scenes.readAloud: It begins with a sound like a sheet being torn and a light like a sunrise, and then the room is on fire from floor to ceiling, a white-orange fire that roars like a train, and the sprinklers come on with a hiss and the fire simply goes on burning under the falling water, and the smoke is yellow and tastes of pennies and you cannot see the door.

skillChecks.success: You reach the steel door or the ventilation shaft with the can, and slam the door behind you. The fire stays in its room, as the vault was built to make it.
skillChecks.failure: 2d6 fire damage and a DC 12 Constitution save against the fumes before you get clear. You still get clear.

skillChecks.success: Out of the Gower gate in a studio car (Bunny's, or one from the transport garage), through the barrier, and gone down Santa Monica Boulevard before the fire engines arrive.
skillChecks.failure: A studio police car follows to the boulevard, then stops at the studio line; a Hollywood Division radio car picks you up instead. Lose it (a second Driving check) or +3 Heat for a chase the police see.

scenes.name: Contact Sheet
scenes.description: Somewhere safe, under a desk lamp, the party looks at the negatives. Let the players describe what they are looking for, and give them the faces. Vivian, if present, names everyone. End the scenario on the last frame: Harlan Shay handing Councilman Fenwick an envelope.
scenes.readAloud: Thirty-one frames, small and reversed, black for white. You hold them up to the lamp with tweezers and a magnifying glass. A card table under a hanging lamp, with a green baize top and chips stacked in towers. A heavy man with a moustache and a councilman's lapel pin accepting an envelope across it. Another man, thinner, counting what is in one. A big pink-faced man with a ring shaking hands with the first. And then, in the last frame on the strip, a slim silver-haired man in a beautiful suit leaning over the table to hand an envelope across, smiling kindly, and beyond him, out of focus, a dark-haired girl laughing at something someone has said.

skillChecks.success: You know the councilmen's faces from the newspapers: Dwight Hollister of the Valley district and Ray Fenwick of the Hollywood district. The pink-faced man is Wendell Haig of Haig Homesites. (Vivian, Percy or Roz know without a roll.)
skillChecks.failure: You do not know the faces. Roz's newspaper morgue, or Percy, or Vivian, will name them in an hour.

encounters: Two studio police (Night Watchmen) and a Guard Dog on the back lot
Shay's men: two Crooked Cops in plain clothes borrowed from Dolan, who want no shooting and will back off if the fire starts
Tiny Bascombe (Bouncer, 22 hit points) and two Street Toughs from the Sirocco, if they followed the party; they will shoot
The nitrate fire (see the vault's secrets) and the Hollywood fire department in six minutes (+2 Heat if a fire is reported, +3 for gunfire)

npcsInvolved.name: Harlan Shay, 52
npcsInvolved.role: The client; the man at the pool
npcsInvolved.description: Grieving, generous, bandaged, more frightened every day. He has not slept since Tuesday. He keeps paying the party because he does not know what else to do, and because if they find the negatives first he may still be able to buy them.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get the negatives. Keep the studio alive. Not think about the three minutes he stood at the edge of the pool. If confronted with three or more K2 clues, see the dmTips.

npcsInvolved.name: Lt. Frank Dolan, 55
npcsInvolved.role: Detective lieutenant, LAPD Hollywood Division; on Shay's payroll
npcsInvolved.description: Big, slow, tidy, grey moustache, doughnut sugar on his tie, a lake cabin at Arrowhead. Has been paid by the studio for six years to make things tidy, and he is very good at it. Not violent unless cornered; he uses other men for that.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep the case closed, keep the money coming, retire in four years.

npcsInvolved.name: Walter Ness, 40
npcsInvolved.description: Wire glasses, three children, a dentist's bill, a conscience. Took $200 and has not slept since either.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Not to lose his job, and somewhere under that, to have done the right thing once.

npcsInvolved.name: Pearl Duchesne, 60
npcsInvolved.role: Chief operator, Hollywood Personal Answering Service
npcsInvolved.description: Reading glasses on a chain, a son in the Navy, and thirty days of everyone's secrets on pink slips.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Mr. Kurland was kind to her for six years. That's enough.

npcsInvolved.name: Mrs. Esperanza Ruiz, 50
npcsInvolved.role: Housekeeper next door; the witness who saw car No. 7
npcsInvolved.description: Widow of a Red Car motorman, knows cars, smokes on the back steps at night, and has been insulted that the police did not bother to ask her anything.

npcsInvolved.name: Lyle Preston, 38
npcsInvolved.role: Investigator for the House committee; red herring
npcsInvolved.description: Thin, pale, barbered, soft-voiced, a briefcase and a Phi Beta Kappa key. Collects names the way other men collect stamps. Had dinner with Shay at the Sirocco on Tuesday night until 10:30.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Names for the October hearings, and leverage over Bernard Castellane. He has heard about the Sirocco and wants the evidence for his own uses.

npcsInvolved.name: Lupe Ortega, 35
npcsInvolved.description: Three mornings a week for four years; knows where every glass goes. Grieving and angry. Will help the party and Vivian with anything.
npcsInvolved.motivation: That someone says out loud that Mr. Abel did not do this to himself.

npcsInvolved.name: Dr. Roland Pryor
npcsInvolved.description: Full sheet in the companion files. The man the party needs for the body, and the man to hide Vivian with.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Patients first. And a professional fury at a coroner who signs a report before he looks.

rewards.money: Shay's $50 a day each continues as long as the party reports, and he offers a $200 bonus each on Wednesday to 'let the police handle Abel'. Tiny's men carry $60 between them. Preston offers no money, only immunity from subpoena.
items: The Sirocco negatives and contact sheet: thirty-one frames (clue M1a for kl-scenario-003)
A reel of Vivian's and Kurland's Dry Wells screen tests, worth nothing and everything to Vivian
The $5,000 currency band, the answering-service call sheets, and Walter Ness's statement if he gave one
Two .38 revolvers and .38 rounds (18) from beaten Sirocco men, if any

twists: The client is the killer. Every K2 clue is honest and points one way. Shay did not plan it; he went up with $5,000 to buy the negatives, hit a man who swung at him, and then stood at the edge of the pool and did not reach in. He is the most sympathetic person the party will ever have to turn in.

The obvious suspect, Lyle Preston of the committee, argued with Kurland on his doorstep at six and is innocent. His alibi is dinner with Harlan Shay, which tells the party the fixer and the committee man are friends.

Vivian's own words on the answering service, 'Then I'll do it without you', are a red herring that hurts. She and Kurland were arguing about whether to expose Haig publicly (her plan) or trade the negatives quietly (his). She is going to have to live with the last thing she said to him.
Kurland hid the evidence in the one building on the lot built to survive a fire, and the evidence can burn the building down.
The negatives show Harlan Shay handing over an envelope. Kurland told him so at the pool. That is why Shay stood still.
dmTips: This is the procedural scenario. Let the players be good at it. Every K clue is core: if they go to the right place and ask, they get it. Rolls give detail (the coffee in the stomach, the teller's description, the woman's voice on the 10:40 call).

If the party confronts Shay with three or more K2 clues, he does not deny he was there. He says: 'He swung at me. He fell. I couldn't get him out.' Insight DC 15 sees that the last sentence is the lie. Then he asks for time, until the premiere, to 'make it right', and offers to testify against Haig and Ambler. He will not run, and he will not hurt the party; he will try to buy them, then beg them. Where he goes from here is the party's choice and drives kl-scenario-004.

If the party stops reporting to Shay, the opposition at the vault is only Tiny's men (if they were followed) or nobody. Reward caution: an unopposed vault job is a quiet triumph and the fire never starts.

Bring Vivian into the investigation. She will insist on seeing Kurland's body, on hearing the answering-service sheets, and on going to the vault. She knows the lot. Her grief turns, over this scenario, into the anger that drives the finale.

Use Lyle Preston to put pressure on the party's own pasts. He has a file on everyone; he is happy to make each of them a little frightened. The committee should feel like weather that is getting worse.
Level-up note: the 1800 XP in this file is per character and takes each character from 3rd to 4th level. Award it at the contact sheet.

Period texture: the 'SUBPOENAED WRITER DROWNS' headline in Thursday's paper with Kurland's studio portrait; the studio's flowers at the funeral home; the World Series coming; a Red Car motorman's widow who knows a Packard by its grille; the smell of nitrate, vinegar and camphor.
